verse: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and a contrite heart, O God, You will not despise.
story: A king who could afford any offering on earth comes to God with empty hands.

David has sinned with Bathsheba, and he knows no bull or ram can cover it. God takes no pleasure in burnt offerings brought to settle the account, he says, or he would bring them. What God asks for is the one thing David has left: a spirit that has stopped defending itself, a heart crushed by what it has done. That, David is sure, God will not turn away. He has already prayed for a clean heart; here he trusts that the broken one is welcome first. The mercy he leans on is the mercy that would one day be opened wide in Christ.
You do not have to mend yourself before you come. Bring Him the truth today; He will not despise it.
theme: Lent: repentance, the road to the cross
